rules.motion-studio-setup:
---
description: Project-local motion studio setup (no global installs)
---
# Motion studio - project-local setup

The public course installs node, ffmpeg and python with Homebrew and `npx skills add ... -g`. In this sandbox everything is local:

- Node packages: `npm init -y` (once), then `npm i -D playwright remotion @remotion/cli` and `npx playwright install chromium` (browsers land in `.ai-sandbox/cache/ms-playwright`).
- ffmpeg without a system package: `npm i -D ffmpeg-static` (exposes a project-local binary) or `./.venv/bin/python -m pip install imageio-ffmpeg`.
- Python audio analysis: `./.venv/bin/python -m pip install numpy librosa soundfile` (Windows: `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip ...`).
- Render with `npx remotion render <Composition> out/<name>.mp4`; preview with `npx remotion studio`. HyperFrames: `npx hyperframes init`, `npx hyperframes render`.
- Never `brew install`, `pip install --user`, `npm i -g`, or `npx skills add -g`; the guard blocks them. Skills are already imported project-locally.
- Package your own pipeline as a skill: `aisb add skill motion-reel --from ./my-skill-dir`, then `aisb pack` to share it.

commands.motion-reel:
---
description: Produce a short motion reel from a brief (spec -> scenes -> render)
argument-hint: "<brief or script file>"
---
You are the motion director for this project. Input: $ARGUMENTS

1. Read DESIGN.md (brand, type, motion tokens) if present.
2. Write a shot list (scene, duration, easing/spring, sound cue) and get confirmation.
3. Implement with the Remotion/HyperFrames skills; keep everything inside this folder; render to out/.
4. Open the render with the playwright MCP server and critique it against the shot list; iterate twice.
5. Summarize what changed and the final render path.

notes: Check each source's license in .ai-sandbox/bundles/bundles.lock.json before redistributing a bundle built from it.
